user.title: Add a Monolith HTP-1
user.description:
Enter the processor's address. It has no username or password — the control interface is unauthenticated, so anyone who can reach it on the network can control it.

There is no discovery: the HTP-1 advertises no mDNS or SSDP service, and its status document carries no MAC address, so Home Assistant cannot follow it if DHCP moves it. Give each unit a reservation or a static address.

data_description.host: Hostname or IP address, for example 192.168.1.50. A pasted http:// URL is accepted too.

reconfigure.title: Change the address
reconfigure.description:
This processor is currently at {host}. Enter its new address.

The unit is identified by its serial number, so pointing this entry at a different processor is refused rather than silently re-targeting every entity.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach that address. Check that the processor is powered on and on the network, and that the address is right.
error.timeout_connect: The address answered but did not complete the connection. The processor accepts network connections while it is still starting up, so wait about thirty seconds and try again.
error.not_htp1: Something answered at that address, but it did not respond like a Monolith HTP-1. Check that the address belongs to the processor.
error.invalid_host: That does not look like an address.
error.unknown: Something unexpected went wrong. Check the Home Assistant log for details.

abort.already_configured: That processor is already set up.
abort.wrong_device: That address belongs to a different processor. To add it, use Add integration instead.

init.title: Options
init.description: These change how the integration behaves. What appears as entities is controlled in the entity settings, not here.

data_description.power_off_action:
What "turn off" should do.

Sleep turns off the front panel and waits for a fast wake-up. The processor stays on the network, so Home Assistant can still see it and can turn it back on. This is the right choice for almost everyone.

Shut down powers the processor down completely. It leaves the network with it, so Home Assistant loses the device entirely and cannot turn it back on — somebody has to press the button on the unit itself.

Do nothing means Home Assistant will never power this processor down, which is worth choosing if a stray automation could silence a room in use.
data_description.max_volume_db: Refuse to set the volume above this level. Leave empty to allow the processor's own maximum. This limits what Home Assistant sends; it does not change what the processor reports.

options.off: Shut down (Home Assistant loses the unit)
